forward.prompt:
These are every image in one clothing SKU. Each VIEW contains an original photograph and a sheet of its SAM3 mask regions. Every mask has a UNIQUE ID beginning with R; IDs never repeat in another view.
Find every visually distinct garment that has visible pixels in an available mask in EVERY VIEW. The same garment may be shown alone, worn, from behind, as a fabric detail, or partly hidden under another layer. Use ALL views to establish identity. Do not require a small visible collar or undershirt strip to have the full garment silhouette. Match by fabric, construction, color and the context. A jacket and its undershirt remain separate garments even if the layers are sewn together. Similar colors alone are insufficient. A mask mixing different garments is not usable. Do not invent unseen pixels or new mask boundaries.
First describe which garments are present and which disappear, using the region IDs printed on the crops. Then output JSON: {"tracks":[{"garment":"description","regions":["R001", "R004", ...]}]}. This is only an output schema, not an answer. List only supplied region IDs and assign each ID to at most one track. A track must cover EVERY VIEW with at least one visible region. Extra fragments of the SAME garment in a view may share a track. Unlisted regions are removed. Keep repeated styling too, if present in every view. Do not select by the item for sale. If nothing is visibly supported everywhere, return an empty tracks list.

The key is to track the same garment across all views by fabric, construction, color, and context — even if it appears in different poses, angles, or partially obscured.

---

### Step-by-step Analysis:

We have 6 views (00 to 05), each with its own set of mask regions.

---

#### View 00: Regions R001–R007
- R001: Top (velvet turtleneck)
- R002: Pants (black leather)
- R003: Hair/neckline (not a garment)
- R004: Shoe (left)
- R005: Bag
- R006: Belt
- R007: Waistband (possibly part of pants or belt)

---

#### View 01: Regions R008–R010
- R008: Top (side view, same velvet turtleneck)
- R009: Pants (side view, same black leather)
- R010: Hair/neckline (not a garment)

---

#### View 02: Regions R011
- R011: Top (front, flat lay — same velvet turtleneck)

---

#### View 03: Regions R012–R013

- R013: Pants (back view, same black leather)

---

#### View 04: Regions R014–R016
- R014: Top (front, hands in pockets — same velvet turtleneck)
- R015: Pants (front, hands in pockets — same black leather)
- R016: Hair/neckline (not a garment)

---

#### View 05: Regions R017–R019
- R017: Top (close-up side — same velvet turtleneck)
- R018: Pants (close-up — same black leather)
- R019: Hair/neckline (not a garment)

---

### Garment Tracking:

We now look for garments that appear in **every view**.

#### 1. Velvet Turtleneck Top
- View 00: R001
- View 01: R008
- View 02: R011
- View 03: R012
- View 04: R014
- View 05: R017

✅ Appears in every view. Consistent fabric (velvet), color (olive/grey), construction (turtleneck, long sleeves). Even in close-ups and flat lay, it’s the same garment.

#### 2. Black Leather Pants
- View 00: R002
- View 01: R009
- View 03: R013
- View 04: R015
- View 05: R018

❌ **Missing in View 02** — View 02 is a flat lay of the top only. No pants are visible. Therefore, **not present in every view**.

#### 3. Belt (R006)
- Only in View 00. Not in any other view.

❌ Not present in every view.

#### 4. Shoes (R004)
- Only in View 00.

❌ Not present in every view.

#### 5. Bag (R005)
- Only in View 00.

❌ Not present in every view.

#### 6. Waistband (R007)
- Only in View 00.

❌ Not present in every view.

#### 7. Hair/Neckline regions (R003, R010, R016, R019)
- Not garments.

---

### Conclusion:

Only **one garment** — the **velvet turtleneck top** — is visible in **every view** (via regions R001, R008, R011, R012, R014, R017).

The black leather pants are not visible in View 02, so they do not qualify.

}
